events.text:
## Recommendation
- Expect slow pier salmon fishing this week everywhere. Rating: St. Joseph 1, Grand Haven 1, Muskegon 0, South Haven 0.
- Go to St. Joseph. It has the only recent pier report that rated good, though its newest pier report was slow.
- Cast spinners and spoons, and use glow spoons in low light. That is what worked on the piers.
- At Grand Haven, alewife on the bottom is the bait that caught coho and Chinook.
- I could not get a wind forecast, so check the wind before you go.

## Why
- St. Joseph is the best bet because the Sept 11 St. Joseph report had pier anglers catching "good numbers of salmon" on spinners and spoons, the only good pier rating in the last four weeks.
- I'd expect the pier to stay slow this week because every pier report since Sept 4 has been rated slow or not rated, including the newest one from Grand Haven and St. Joseph (Sept 25).
- Grand Haven is second because its pier anglers caught coho and Chinook on alewives in the Sept 4 and Sept 11 reports.
- South Haven and Muskegon rank lowest because their latest pier reports were slow (South Haven Sept 18, Muskegon Sept 18), and South Haven had no pier report on Sept 25.

## Evidence
**Recent reports** (newest is 6 days old, Sept 25)
- St. Joseph, Sept 25: "The piers were also slow for salmon." Quality 0.
- St. Joseph, Sept 11: "Pier anglers were catching good numbers of salmon and an occasional steelhead… Most fish were caught by casting spinners and spoons." Quality 3. Water was 69 F, -1 F over the week.
- Grand Haven, Sept 25: "Pier anglers found the salmon action to be slow, however a few were caught casting glow spoons in low light conditions." Quality 0.
- Grand Haven, Sept 4 and Sept 11: pier anglers caught coho and Chinook "on alewives and while casting glow spoons." Not rated (Chinook rated 1 on Sept 4).
- Muskegon, Sept 18: "Pier anglers casting for salmon were unsuccessful." Quality 0. Sept 11 pier was 1, with glow spoons.
- South Haven, Sept 18: "Pier fishing was very slow for salmon." Quality 0. Sept 4 and Sept 11 were also slow.

**Past seasons** (similar weeks near 65 F, mid-September to mid-October)
- St. Joseph, Oct 5 2022 and Oct 11 2023: piers slow for salmon.
- Grand Haven, Oct 4 2023: "No salmon were reported to be caught from the piers."
- South Haven, Oct 11 2023: piers closed due to poor weather. This is a real risk in October.
- Past seasons mostly show slow piers at this temperature, with occasional good weeks.

**Conditions now** (buoy readings for the week before Oct 1; live data and wind forecast were unavailable)
- St. Joseph (buoy 45026): 68 F, -1 F over the week.
- Grand Haven and Muskegon (buoy 45029): 65 F, -6 F over the week. That sharp drop can signal upwelling, which could bring fish to the piers.
- South Haven: 65 F, -6 F. The tool reported this figure from buoy 45029, not the South Haven buoy, so treat it with caution.
- The modeled pierhead water temperature and cold-layer depth were not returned.

## Caveats
- The newest report is 6 days old (Sept 25), and it is the only one covering the current week. The ratings above are estimates from older reports.
- Buoy temperatures are measured but miles offshore. I could not get the modeled pierhead temperature, so I can't confirm upwelling at the piers.
- Muskegon and South Haven have no pier report for Sept 25, so their ratings rest on older data.
- Check the wind and the pier status before you leave. Past October reports show piers closed by bad weather.

## Sources
- Sept 25 bulletin: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3b7fd3a
- Sept 18 bulletin: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3b67fce
- Sept 11 bulletin: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3b5093d
- Sept 4 bulletin: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3b2f6aa
- Past-season bulletins used: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3754df7 (Oct 11 2023), https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/37424d6 (Oct 4 2023), https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/330b601 (Oct 5 2022)
